result:
Understood. I'll keep this to one short step before the write-up: how it gets built. You've described what you want, not how to build it, so I'll make that call. Here are the two real options and my pick.

**A. Add it to the taproom app (my pick).** Batch tracking becomes a new section of the Flask app you already run on the office Pi, with its own tables in the same SQLite database. Brewers open a page on a tablet or PC in the brewhouse. A USB barcode scanner types the sack's lot number into the form, so nobody has to touch a keyboard with wet hands. The label printer prints batch number and bottling date from the bottling page. There's still one thing to run, back up and keep alive. The cost is that the taproom and the brewhouse share one app, so a broken update to one could take down the other.

**B. A separate small app on the same Pi.** It works the same way for the brewers, but it has its own database file and runs on its own. Taproom changes can never touch your trace records. The cost is two apps to update and two databases to back up.

I'd go with A. You already keep that app running, and the tracking records are simple enough that sharing it carries little risk. If keeping recall records fully apart from the tabs matters more to you, say so and I'll switch to B.

This is a full project, so I'll write it as a design document. A reviewer will read it first, and I may come back once with a few questions.
